question.problem:
The following table shows some values of a continuous function $f(x)$ over the interval $[0,10].$

| $x$ | $0$ | $3$ | $5$ | $7$ | $10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $4$ | $5$ | $9$ | $15$ |

Use the left Riemann sum, with the four subintervals indicated by the data, to approximate the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ over the interval $[0,10].$
question.worked_solution:
In this case, we have $n=4$ rectangles. Using the left Riemann sum, the area is approximated as

$$
A≈f(0)Δ{x}_{1}+f(3)Δ{x}_{2}+f(5)Δ{x}_{3}+f(7)Δ{x}_{4},
$$

where each $Δ{x}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $x$-value and the next one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i+1}-{x}_{i}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δx$'s.

| $x$ | $0$ | $3$ | $5$ | $7$ | $10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δx$ | $3$ | $2$ | $2$ | $3$ | $-$ |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $4$ | $5$ | $9$ | $15$ |

Finally, we plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈1\cdot 3+4\cdot 2+5\cdot 2+9\cdot 3 \\  & =3+8+10+27 \\  & =48.\end{aligned}
$$
